matches.rationale: GT 1 concerns the abstract claiming T = exp(O(log d/ε)) = d^(O(1/ε)) when the actual bound is d^(O(1/ε²)). Pred 1 discusses a mismatch between ρ and Rate(P,||·||) in Theorem 1.1 vs Corollary C.5, which is a different issue about notation consistency rather than the exponent being wrong.

GT 2 concerns the abstract claiming tightness between upper and lower bounds when there's a polynomial gap in exponents (1/6 vs 1/ε²). Pred 5 discusses inconsistencies in lower bound exponents but focuses on d^{1/7} vs d^{1/14} and ε^{-1/6} vs ε^{-1/7}, not the gap between upper and lower bounds.
GT 3 concerns a fabricated citation '[ZKL23]' in the introduction that doesn't appear in references. None of the findings mention missing or fabricated citations.
GT 4 concerns the Bregman divergence definition having reversed arguments (D_R(y || p) := R(p) - R(y) instead of R(y) - R(p)). None of the findings identify this specific error in Section 2.3.
GT 5 concerns the claim that TreeCal doesn't require knowledge of ρ when it actually does for parameter setting. None of the findings address this misrepresentation about implementation requirements.

GT 6 concerns contradictory statements about whether TreeCal is 'nearly identical' to prior work vs. being a novel instantiation. None of the findings identify this coherence issue in the introduction.
GT 7 concerns the misleading claim that ℓ2 calibration bounds are 'independent of d' when diam(P) depends on d. None of the findings address this specific misleading statement.
GT 8 concerns the strong convexity definition having the wrong inequality direction (≥ instead of ≤). None of the findings identify this error in Section 2.4.
GT 9 concerns the overstatement 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem' in the introduction. None of the findings identify this rhetorical exaggeration.
GT 10 concerns Theorem C.1 having constant 1 instead of 3 in the swap regret bound. None of the findings identify this specific numerical error in the theorem statement.
GT 11 concerns missing funding disclosure for Google Research affiliations. None of the findings address ethical or disclosure issues.
GT 12 concerns logical inconsistency about BTL being 'unimplementable' yet having its regret discussed practically. None of the findings identify this coherence issue.
GT 13 concerns misattribution of TreeSwap as 'novel' when it's from prior work [DDFG24, PR24]. None of the findings address this attribution issue.

GT 14 concerns Claim C.3 having a reversed inequality (≤ instead of ≥) in equation (9). Pred 2 identifies exactly this issue in equation (11) of Claim C.3, noting the inequality direction appears reversed and should be ≥ not ≤.
GT 15 concerns overstating generality by claiming results work for 'arbitrary convex set P' when central symmetry is required. None of the findings identify this limitation.
GT 16 concerns missing computational complexity analysis despite claiming TreeCal is 'highly efficient'. None of the findings address this omission.
GT 17 concerns the calibration error definition using ∑_t x_t(p)/T instead of ∑_t x_t(p) in Section 2.1. None of the findings identify this error in the definition.

GT 18 concerns Theorem 4.3 having exponent 1/7 instead of 1/14 on d in the lower bound. Pred 5 identifies this exact inconsistency, noting Theorem 4.3 mentions both 1/7 and 1/14 as exponents on d, which is the corruption described.
